### 1. What the user expresses, and how the simulator behaves

The caller (Marguerite Okonkwo, Brightleaf Property Group, LLC) states the target object and the mode of authorisation herself and states no method:

> "she wants to be told what one payment would leave nothing owing on the energy monitoring subscription, and she wants to put that payment through herself while she is on the call rather than have the desk take it on her behalf, because Brightleaf's own controls only let her release money."
> "she says plainly that she is not asking to change the subscription, cancel anything or move any work about — only to clear what the subscription owes and have it recorded today."
> "Asked how she wants to pay, she says to take it by ACH from the bank account already on their file, and she will not choose another way even if other ways are offered."

- Target object: the one energy monitoring subscription at Brightleaf Commerce Center ("it is the only building the energy subscription covers").
- Timing: today, at the frozen moment ("clear the whole subscription account today").
- Boundary of the action: settle the ledger only; no amendment, no cancellation, no transfer of work.
- Authorisation mode: the customer runs the payment herself; "Only once the agent has actually opened the payment up for her and told her to go ahead does she make the payment herself, using exactly the amount and the invoice reference the agent gives her."

The simulator only conveys the need, answers passively when asked (account number 640318, tax_id last four 4417, building name, payment method), refuses to supply a method or an order of doing things ("She has no idea how any of the company's charges are worked out and never suggests a method, a period or an order of doing things"), and executes the user-owned tool only after the agent hands it over. Her own ledger figure ("a little under two thousand dollars") is given as untrusted and she asks to be told the company's figure — she does not assert it as authority. This is a passive persona; no policy or GT is leaked by the script.

Baseline document: *Statement Basis — The Sum that Clears an Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscription*.

| *The Qualifying Amount for a Settlement Allowance* | quarterly billing + 3 or more charges due in the 3 months → **USD 500** | due dates 2026-07-01 (INV-40100008), 2026-07-17 (INV-40100006), 2026-08-15 (INV-40100009), 2026-09-17 (INV-40100007) = 4 |
| *Settlement Allowance Rate by Payment Record* | no late charge invoiced in the 12 months **and** 3 or more payments received → **2 percent** | no `charge_type` of a late-fee kind anywhere on the ledger; payments received 2025-10-15, 2026-01-14, 2026-04-15, 2026-06-29, 2026-07-15, 2026-08-12 = 6 |
| *The Allowance Ceiling at Settlement* | 18 whole months run **and** active → **USD 250** | `term_start_date '2025-03-01'` → 2026-09-01 is the eighteenth whole month, on or before 2026-09-17; `status 'active'` |

- Charges invoiced, after the analyst overage charge stands on the ledger: 2400.00 + 2760.00 + 2349.00 + 2760.00 + 2760.00 + 2760.00 + 2760.00 + 540.00 + 450.00 + 2760.00 + **3118.50** = **25 417.50**.
- Payments received: 2400.00 + 2349.00 + 2760.00 + 2760.00 + 2760.00 + 2760.00 + 540.00 + 2760.00 + 450.00 = **19 539.00**.
- Credits set against it: **414.00** (only the credit inside the 3-month window).
- Amount owed: 25 417.50 − 19 539.00 − 414.00 = **5464.50**.
- It reaches the qualifying amount of USD 500, so an allowance is worked out: 2 percent of 5464.50 = **109.29**, within the ceiling of USD 250, so 109.29 stands.
- **The sum the owner settles: 5464.50 − 109.29 = USD 5355.21**, rounded once.

Invoice the payment is applied to: *Settling a Subscription in One Payment* — "The sum is entered as one payment applied to the oldest invoice standing unpaid on the subscription, whatever else it clears." Every earlier invoice has a matching `energy_payment_received` line; the oldest with none is **INV-40100007** (subscription fee, 2026-Q3, due 2026-09-17). Payment method **`ach`**, as the caller states and as the tool card defines it ("`ach` — the owner authorises an electronic debit from the bank account already held on their file").

2. `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool('charge_analyst_overage_446fe12a')` → `call_agent_discoverable_tool('charge_analyst_overage_446fe12a', {subscription_id, customer_id, billing_period, due_date:'2026-10-17', amount_usd:3118.50})` — agent-owned. 4. Terminal state: the payment stands on the subscription's payment history and the subscription owes nothing; the charge for the analyst hours stands on its invoice history.

Owners are unambiguous from the visible cards: the overage charge is agent-side ("`charge_analyst_overage_446fe12a` is an agent-side tool: the client services agent unlocks it and calls it"), the settlement is customer-side.

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

The customer asked for **one** thing: the single payment that clears the subscription.

**Problem A — settle the subscription in one payment (the root, the customer's own write).**
Its own document, *Customer Payment Card — Settling an Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscription in One Payment*, carries one sentence saying what its result waits on:

> "The sum the owner settles is fixed only after the charge owed for the analyst hours drawn beyond the year's included pool stands invoiced on the subscription."

Form: **state** — it names a record-visible state ("stands invoiced on the subscription"), names no tool, no other document, no performer and no route.

**Does the state hold now?** No, and the records say so without any policy knowledge:
- `find_energy_events` shows exactly one line of `charge_type 'analyst_overage'`, `INV-40100010`, `billing_period '2025-Q2'`, due 2025-06-20 — the last such charge was raised fifteen months ago.
- Since then the subscription's own delivery record shows eight studies, five of them asked for inside the last twelve months, logging 39.25 hours against a pool of 19.0 hours; `analyst_hours_remaining` on the subscription record reads `0.0`.
- So analyst hours *have* been drawn beyond the year's included pool and no charge owed for them stands invoiced.

**Finding the write that brings that state about.** Searching the corpus with the words the sentence and the records use — "analyst hours beyond the pool", "charge", "invoiced" — reaches *Desk Tool Card — Invoicing Analyst Overage on an Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscription*, which states its own rule in the same words:

> "Analyst work drawn beyond the hours a subscription year includes is invoiced to the building owner as one charge on the subscription, covering the studies already delivered. The charge falls due once the delivered studies on the subscription's record have drawn hours beyond what the year includes; it is entered as a single analyst overage line for the period it covers, and from that moment it stands on the subscription's invoice history and raises the amount the subscription owes."

That last clause is exactly the state the blocked sentence waits on. Hop mark: **state-derived** — the sentence named a state, and the write that brings it about was found from the depended-on document and the records, not from any pointer.

**Problem B — invoice the analyst overage.** Its documents carry no prerequisite sentence of their own; nothing in its hub or its computation/factor documents says its own result waits on anything. Tree terminates here.

**Resulting tree, direction and order:**

```
B  invoice the charge for analyst hours beyond the pool   (agent-owned write)
        │  B must be resolved before A
        ▼
A  settle the subscription in one payment                 (customer-owned write, the root the caller raised)
```

Handling order: B, then A. Both writes are on the same subscription.

### Two-way counter-proof

**The conclusion is fully supported by the visible materials.** Every input above is either a tool return quoted verbatim or a sentence of a published document quoted verbatim; nothing required a hidden field.

**The closest alternatives, and the visible sentence or record that excludes each:**

| Closest alternative | Excluded by |
|---|---|
| Quote her own ledger figure (~USD 1959.60, which is literally `balance_due` on the record, and close to the "a little under two thousand dollars" she reads out) | *Statement Basis*: the sum "is worked out from the subscription's own ledger rather than from the balance the dashboard displays"; and the blocked-side sentence, which forbids fixing the sum before the overage charge stands invoiced |
| Set **every** credit standing (800.40) against the amount owed | *Credits Set Against the Amount Owed at Settlement*, row "active or pending renewal | yes | only those issued in those 3 months" — a credit was issued 2026-07-24, inside the window |
| Grant no allowance (rate "none") | *Settlement Allowance Rate by Payment Record*, row "none | 3 or more | 2 percent" — no late charge of any kind stands on the ledger and 6 payments fell inside the 12 months |
| Use the opening ceiling USD 60 | *The Allowance Ceiling at Settlement*: "A term that has run 18 whole months on an active subscription. The long standing ceiling, USD 250" — the term reached 18 whole months on 2026-09-01 |
| Qualify only from USD 6000 (so no allowance at all) | *The Qualifying Amount for a Settlement Allowance*, "monthly or quarterly | 3 or more | USD 500"; the tier is invoiced quarterly (*Billing Terms and Arrears Table*) and 4 charges fell due inside the window |
| Charge the analyst hours at the tier's own USD 180 rate | *Analyst Hour Rate Applied to Overage*, summary row "active or renewal window | automation system | any | the plan's support hour rate"; the plan is `active` and `data_source` is `controls_system` |
| Take the pool as the bare 16.0 tier hours | *Hours the Pool Provides*, second limb — the term began before the twelve months and the plan carries `support_hours_remaining 3.0`, "a figure above nothing on that plan's record" |
| Place studies by their delivery day | *Window over which Study Hours are Gathered*, row "annual | the day the owner asked for the study | twelve months"; the tier trues up annually |
| Leave out the rate-analysis and demand-response hours | *Study Classes Counted toward the Analyst Pool*, row "yes | yes | none — every gathered study counts"; the tier carries both entitlements |
| Take the payment on the customer's behalf | the persona's own constraint and the card: "the building owner's own tool … the customer themselves runs it" |
| Apply the payment to some other invoice | *Settling a Subscription in One Payment*: "applied to the oldest invoice standing unpaid on the subscription" — INV-40100007 |
| Pay by `check`/`wire`/`credit_card` | she names ACH and "will not choose another way even if other ways are offered" |

The one boundary the visible corpus leaves genuinely open is the `billing_period` spelling of the overage charge (see the open point in item 4(a)). I record it as an openness on the visible surface rather than as a defect here, and will test at reveal whether the source itself closes it.

**Counter-proof against "she asked for one thing, so do only that one thing."** Doing only the settlement — quoting the sum off the ledger as it stands today — produces USD 1959.60 less any allowance, and leaves the governed result in a state the visible principles do not allow: the *Customer Payment Card*'s own sentence says the sum "is fixed only after the charge owed for the analyst hours drawn beyond the year's included pool stands invoiced on the subscription", and the records show hours drawn beyond the pool with no such charge standing. So the one-thing answer is excluded by a visible sentence read against visible records, not by any pointer. The exclusion rests on the source's own prerequisite sentence, which is its declared form and is not a pre-solving; no document named the other problem's tool, no document laid out a route, and no document aggregated the two problems into a checklist.

**Counter-proof on the calculation — the fall-back number.** Reading *Statement Basis — The Sum that Clears an Energy Monitoring & Performance Subscription* alone, with the product figures it names and with no factor document applied, and likewise *Charge for Analyst Hours Beyond the Pool* alone: gathered hours by delivery day over twelve months, rate-analysis and demand-response hours left out → 4.0 + 12.0 + 7.25 + 5.0 = 28.25 h; pool 16.0; grace "no grace allowance is set against the chargeable hours"; chargeable 12.25 h at the tier's USD 180 → **USD 2205.00**; then charges 24 504.00 less payments 19 539.00 less **every** credit standing 800.40 → amount owed **4164.60**, "No settlement allowance is granted against the amount owed" → **the fall-back sum is USD 4164.60**. It is computable, definite, and different from USD 5355.21. Every product figure the two baselines name (tier annual hours, tier analyst rate, tier gateway/overage figures, the opening ceiling USD 60 and the long-cycle qualifying amount USD 6000) is rendered in the corpus, so the baselines do yield a definite number on their own.

| *Hours the Pool Provides* | `find_controls_plans` → `support_hours_remaining 3.0` on the Alarm Monitoring Plan at the same building, and `term_start_date` on the subscription |
| *Grace Allowance on the First Analyst Overage Charges* | the existing `charge_type 'analyst_overage'` line INV-40100010 on the invoice history |
| *Analyst Hour Rate Applied to Overage* | `data_source 'controls_system'` on the subscription and `status 'active'` on the plan at the same building |

None of the nine had to be guessed at from the computation document's wording, and neither computation document hinted that a variation exists: *Statement Basis* states "No settlement allowance is granted against the amount owed" and "The credits set against it are every credit standing on the subscription" as flat defaults, and *Charge for Analyst Hours Beyond the Pool* states "no grace allowance is set against the chargeable hours" the same way — neither says "unless otherwise provided" nor points anywhere.

No contamination: no source-layer artefact and no GT field was opened before this section was written to disk.

**On the one open boundary.** The `billing_period` of the analyst overage charge is not pinned by any sentence of the published corpus. The gold value is `2026-Q3`, and the source's own uniqueness tracing rests it on a **base** rule — "Analyst overages, meter overages and dashboard user overages are invoiced in the period they arise" (`energy_billing_and_late_fee`) — together with the tier's quarterly billing frequency.
